title: 1955 AHSME Problem 43
statement: The pairs of values of \(x\) and \(y\) that are the common solutions of the equations \(y=(x+1)^2\) and \(xy+y=1\) are:

solutions.text:
Substitution into \(y(x+1)=1\) gives \[ (x+1)^3=1. \] The three cube roots of \(1\) consist of one real root and two nonreal roots. Each determines exactly one corresponding value \(y=(x+1)^2.\) Therefore there is one real pair and two imaginary pairs.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Substitute \(y=(x+1)^2\) to obtain a cubic in \(x+1\)
